transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. When can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a full month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that information. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. If you were using eye gel or drops for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

However, if you need a new supply, your GP should be able to provide some more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That’s helpful, thank you. I’ve also noticed I’m very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Yes, that's quite normal. It's common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you have significant pain in bright light, or your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, that’s reassuring. My last question is, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

How long ago was your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's been about a week since my surgery. Thank you for the information; it’s good to know what to expect. I don't have any more questions for now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's good to know – you're still in that early stage where some blurriness is quite normal, so that should improve soon.

Just to confirm, have all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've answered all my questions. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and best wishes with your recovery!
